audit_findings.title: Post-FY2025 borrowing is not charged against the earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: Debt increased $448.1 million and cash increased $366.3 million from 2025 year-end to 2026-06-28; the $450 million 5.875% notes carry a $26.4 million annual coupon, or $5.9 million more than the subsequently redeemed $350 million notes; the $350 million redemption cash equals $2.49 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: June cash is added in the equity bridge while the FY2025 OE anchor contains neither the incremental recurring interest nor a reduction for cash committed to the July debt redemption.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 28, 2025, our total consolidated indebtedness was approximately $1.7 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing mismatch. ATI used $350 million of the June cash shortly afterward to redeem the 2027 notes, so that amount was not continuing excess cash. The remaining $100 million net principal increase adds about $5.9 million of annual pre-tax interest absent from the anchor. Removing the transient cash and recognizing the incremental coupon could reduce scenario values by roughly $2.94-$3.18 per share before tax effects, a material change to the quoted values and buy-below threshold.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the bridge pro forma for the July 8 redemption using cash reduced by $350 million and debt reduced by $350 million, then reduce forward OE for the recurring after-tax incremental interest and issuance-cost amortization on the net additional financing.

audit_findings.title: Parent earnings may be paired with consolidated cash-flow components and cash belonging to NCI
audit_findings.magnitude: $40.9 million of bridge cash attributable to the 40% NCI, computed from $102.3 million of STAL cash; $0.29 per ATI share; OE-component effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds consolidated cash to value attributable to ATI shareholders, while OE may combine parent-attributable income with 100% consolidated D&A, capital spending, and working-capital changes.
audit_findings.evidence: The minority ownership interest is recognized in the consolidated statement of operations as net income attributable to noncontrolling interests, and as equity attributable to the noncontrolling interests within total stockholders’ equity.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash mismatch is demonstrated: 40% of STAL's filed $102.3 million cash balance represents $40.9 million attributable economically to NCI, only about 0.6% of base equity value. The larger OE issue remains unresolved because STAL-specific D&A, maintenance capex, and working-capital figures are not supplied; consolidated add-backs could overstate OE, while consolidated deductions could understate it. Materiality therefore cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild 2025 OE using ATI's 60% economic share of every STAL cash-flow component and rerun the bridge after excluding $40.9 million of NCI-attributable STAL cash.

audit_findings.title: The latest-actual anchor may perpetuate an abnormal mixture of charges and credits
audit_findings.magnitude: $70 million net pre-tax charges, equal to 17.0% of the $412.5 million anchor; a full-dollar adjustment would move scenario values by $5.30-$8.26 per share before tax effects
audit_findings.mechanism: Classification of temporary charges, temporary credits, and recurring costs changes normalized OE and therefore every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Results for fiscal year 2025 included $70 million of net pre-tax charges and fiscal year 2024 included $17 million of net pre-tax gains as further described in the Results of Operations section below.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved normalization issue, not a demonstrated error. The filed $70 million net amount is large relative to the anchor, and treating it differently could alter the scenario values by approximately 14%-15% before tax effects. Direction is mixed because genuine one-time charges depress the current anchor, temporary credits inflate it, and recurring items such as receivables-financing costs must remain deducted.
audit_findings.action: Produce an itemized 2025 OE ledger showing each charge and credit, its tax effect, cash or noncash character, recurrence evidence, and current valuation treatment; rerun all scenarios using only economically justified adjustments.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest can escape an equity-level OE calculation
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.6 million in FY2025, equal to 2.6% of the anchor and $0.80-$1.25 per share of scenario sensitivity before tax effects
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized interest bypasses current net income and would overstate OE if it is also absent from the maintenance-capex deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense in fiscal years 2025 and 2024 was reduced by $10.6 million and $11.8 million, respectively, related to interest capitalization on large, strategic capital projects.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates capitalization, but not double omission from OE. Even if the entire $10.6 million were missing, the computed effect is about 2.2%-2.3% of the scenario values and does not alter the valuation conclusion relative to the $210.65 market price. It is therefore not material on the supplied scale, although the calculation should still deduct the cost exactly once.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $10.6 million through PP&E additions and the maintenance-capex calculation; if excluded, deduct it once from OE and document the corresponding tax treatment.

audit_findings.title: Recurring receivables-financing costs could be wrongly stripped as special charges
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.8 million total FY2025 receivables-sale losses, including $5.3 million from recurring customer programs; 1.9% of the anchor and $0.59-$0.92 per share of scenario sensitivity before tax effects
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding recurring receivables-sale losses back as special charges raises normalized OE and its terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The costs associated with these transactions of $5.3 million, $6.0 million and $6.3 million are reflected in the Company’s consolidated statement of operations for the fiscal years ended December 28, 2025, December 29, 2024 and December 31, 2023, respectively, and are excluded from segment results.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that these costs recur, but the supplied record does not demonstrate that the valuation actually added them back. Even if all $7.8 million were wrongly restored, the computed effect is only about 1.6%-1.7% of scenario value and cannot change the valuation conclusion relative to the market price.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the 2025 OE adjustment ledger and ensure all $7.8 million of receivables-sale losses remain deducted; if any amount was restored, reverse the add-back and rerun the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Committed but unrecognized finance leases may add another senior claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Once the leases commence, their recurring interest must reduce equity-level OE; principal remains context-only under the stated methodology.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon payment of the final progress payments by the lenders, finance leases will commence, and $72.3 million, discounted using the applicable discount rates at lease inceptions, of ROU assets and lease liabilities will be recognized by the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: At FY2025 the filed $72.3 million lease liability was committed but not yet recognized, making this forward-looking rather than a demonstrated omission. The June 2026 record does not establish whether the leases commenced or what recurring interest applies. Because the valuation does not deduct debt principal, only the unprovided interest cost can affect value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain lease-commencement dates, applicable discount rates, and the June or September 2026 finance-lease rollforward; once commenced, confirm the liability is included in debt context and incorporate its recurring after-tax interest into forward OE.
